dimension: Historical Kerala / India reservoir and flood data, especially pre-2020 (Idukki, Idamalayar, Periyar basin)
key_findings: BIGGEST WIN - nwdp.nwic.gov.in is a live CKAN 2.x instance with a fully open API, NO registration and NO API key. `GET /api/3/action/package_list` returns 555 packages (verified 200). `package_show?id=<slug>` gives direct CSV URLs. This is the single most underused door into Indian hydrology and it is nowhere in the AquaSync data loader today.

GENUINE PRE-2020 PERIYAR GAUGE DATA EXISTS AND I DOWNLOADED IT. CWC Kerala daily discharge, two CSVs (39.4 MB + 23.7 MB), 351,607 rows, 40 stations. Three Periyar gauges: NEELEESWARAM (10.18361,76.49556) 1971-2025 with 19,362 daily values; VANDIPERIYAR (9.57333,77.09056); ARANGALI (10.28611,76.32222). Neeleeswaram is the exact CWC G&D site AquaSync routes to above Aluva.

HONEST KILLER CAVEAT - the Neeleeswaram gauge FAILED during the 2018 flood peak. August 2018 has only 18 of 31 days; days 16,17,18,19,20,21,22 are all blank. Last reading before the gap is 6166.426 m3/s on 15-08-2018 09:15; next is 924.282 on 23-08-2018. The all-time top-5 at this gauge are 6323.5 (05-08-2013), 6166.4 (15-08-2018), 4620.7 (09-08-2018), 4452.0 (09-08-2019), 3309.9 (10-08-2018). CWC's own report states the true 2018 peak was ~8800 cumec - i.e. the peak was never measured.

RAT 3.0 Kerala (CWRDM + Univ. of Washington, NASA-funded) publishes per-dam CSVs as PLAIN STATIC FILES at predictable URLs - no login, no scraping. `/assets/RAT_results/{inflow,outflow,aec,sarea_tmsos,dels,evaporation}/{dam}.csv`. Idukki and Idamalayar daily inflow run 2015-10-24 to 2025-02-22 (3410 days), which DOES cover August 2018. Dam slugs are lowercase: `idukki`, `idamalayaar` (note the double-a).

RAT's 2018 Idukki inflow is NOT a substitute for observed data. I compared it to CWC: RAT peaks at 1104.6 m3/s on 2018-08-18; CWC observed 2532 cumec at 22:00 on 15-08-2018. That is 2.3x too low AND 3 days late. The RAT paper admits it: 'Inflow peaks are found to be underpredicted in the case of Idukki, Idamalayaar, and Kakki, requiring bias correction.' Published skill for Idukki, May-Oct 2018 vs KSEB observed: VIC natural inflow r=0.80, RMSE 170.3 m3/s, MAE 115.1, KGE 0.59, NSE 0.603; ResORR-regulated r=0.84, RMSE 153.17, KGE 0.63, NSE 0.68. The dashboard CSV is the plain VIC series (NSE ~0.60), not the better ResORR one.

CWC WEEKLY RESERVOIR BULLETINS ARE THE ONLY REAL, OFFICIAL, NUMERIC 2018 IDUKKI LEVEL+STORAGE RECORD I could actually retrieve. Idukki and Idamalayar are both listed. Verified extractions: 01-08-2018 Idukki 730.25 m / 1.338 BCM / 92%; 23-08-2018 731.69 m / 1.417 BCM / 97%; 30-08-2018 730.50 m / 1.352 BCM / 93%. FRL 732.43 m and live cap 1.460 BCM in the bulletin match AquaSync's constants exactly - a free cross-check.

45 of the 52 weekly 2018 bulletins are downloadable, BUT the two covering the flood are missing from the archive listing: 2018-08-09 and 2018-08-16 (also missing 03-29, 05-10, 09-27, 10-18, 12-27). I tried 7 filename variants for those two - all 404. So weekly resolution exists for 2018 but with a hole precisely over the event.

IMD 0.25-degree daily gridded rainfall downloads in ONE unauthenticated line, no registration, no key: `curl -X POST -d "RF25=2018" https://www.imdpune.gov.in/cmpg/Griddata/RF25.php -o RF25_2018.nc`. Verified: HTTP 200, 25,431,832 bytes, NetCDF classic, RAINFALL(365,129,135) mm, lat 6.5-38.5, lon 66.5-100.0. Nearest cell to Idukki is 9.75N/77.0E; Aug 2018 there reads 203.5 mm on the 9th, 153.3 and 201.8 mm on the 15th-16th, annual total 4048.9 mm. Coverage 1901-2024.

GUARDIAN is the answer to the Muskingum K/x calibration gap (gap #2), though NOT to the 2018 gap. It publishes HOURLY monsoon discharge for 210 Indian CWC stations from 2020 to present, derived from the CWC flood portal water-surface-elevation feed via rating curves. All three Periyar gauges are included with published rating curve coefficients: NEELEESWARAM monsoon cubic-poly p1=10.698 p2=198.767 p3=33.540, NSE 0.765, RMSE 170.7 m3/s from N=2273; non-monsoon NSE 0.786, RMSE 127.5, N=6552. Hourly Neeleeswaram from 2020 overlaps the amith-vp KSEB release feed (2020-08-13 on) - that is a directly usable inflow/outflow pair for Muskingum fitting.

THE 2018 6-HOURLY IDUKKI HYDROGRAPH EXISTS ONLY AS A FIGURE, NOT A TABLE - in two places. (a) CWC 'Kerala Floods August 2018' report Fig.4 'Inflow, Outflow and Water Level: Idukki Reservoir'. Its x-axis tick labels ARE extractable as PDF text (09-08-18 12:00 through 18-08-18 06:00 at 7-hour steps), so the chart is a vector Excel plot and the series are recoverable by path extraction, not just pixel digitising. (b) Current Science 116(5):780-794 Fig.6a (Sudheer et al. 2019), 6-hourly, no data table anywhere in its 15 pages. Both papers got their numbers from KSEB directly.

THE REAL ROUTE TO GENUINE 2018 DATA IS AN EMAIL, NOT AN API. Three independent teams state they obtained in-situ Idukki/Idamalayar 2018 inflow from KSEB: Suresh et al. 2024 ('manually calibrated with respect to in-situ inflow data obtained from the KSEB for Idamalayaar reservoir', and Table 5 compares against 'Observed inflow from KSEB for the period of May - October 2018'); Sudheer et al. 2019 acknowledge KSEB and CWRDM Kottayam; the CWC report used KSEB gate logs. CWRDM (cwrdm.kerala.gov.in, 200) co-developed RAT-Kerala and is a Kerala state institution - it is the most tractable single point of contact, and RAT-Kerala already proves a data-sharing channel exists.

Kerala SW manual daily rainfall 1991-2020 (24.2 MB, 151,429 rows) is real and covers 2018 (8,435 station-days), but only TWO stations have long records inside the Idukki catchment: BOYCE ESTATE (9.56472,76.91056) 2000-2020 continuously, 176 days in 2018; and Vannapuram (9.93611,76.46333) 2002-2020, 189 days in 2018. Neriyamangalam and Boothathankettu - the two stations actually on the Periyar main stem - exist in the file but ONLY for 2011. Treat the River/Basin/Tributary columns as garbage: Kerala stations are labelled with rivers 'Narmada', 'Tapi', 'Luni', 'Mahi', 'Banas'. Lat/lon and station names are sound.

sources.name: National Water Data Portal (NWDP) CKAN API
sources.what_it_provides: Open CKAN 2.x API over 555 datasets from CWC, CGWB and every state water department. No registration, no API key, no rate limit hit in ~40 calls. Endpoints used and verified: /api/3/action/package_list, /api/3/action/package_show?id=<slug>, /api/3/action/status_show. Resource CSVs are direct, unauthenticated downloads.
sources.relevance: high - this is the single highest-value new door for AquaSync; it is how you reach every Periyar gauge series below, and it can be wired into the existing data loader in a day
sources.last_activity: live; Kerala and CWC resources carry 2026-2030 forward files, so it is actively maintained
sources.caveat: Dataset titles routinely lie about temporal coverage (see the Kerala SW discharge entry). Always download and histogram the date column before believing a title. The geographic hierarchy columns (River/Basin/Tributary) are corrupted by a bad join across the whole portal.

sources.name: CWC Kerala daily river discharge 2001-2025 (NWDP resource)
sources.what_it_provides: 39,425,558 bytes, 217,538 rows, 40 Kerala CWC gauging stations. Periyar rows = 30,833. NEELEESWARAM 8,478 records 2001-2025 (284 in 2018); VANDIPERIYAR 14,837 (568 in 2018, twice-daily 08:00 and 08:30); ARANGALI 7,518 (173 in 2018). Columns include Station, Latitude, Longitude, 'Data Acquisition Time' (DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM), 'Manual Daily River Water Discharge (m3/sec)'.
sources.relevance: high - genuine observed Periyar discharge covering 2018 and the whole pre-2020 period; the downstream validation target AquaSync currently has no observations for
sources.caveat: VERIFIED HOLE: Neeleeswaram August 2018 is missing days 5,12,16,17,18,19,20,21,22,24,25,26,27 - the flood peak (16-22 Aug) is entirely absent. Arangali is missing 16-27 Aug. Record density also decays: Neeleeswaram had 365 days in 2001-2004 but only 276-335 per year after 2023. Timestamps are single instantaneous readings, not daily means.

sources.name: CWC Kerala daily river discharge 1950-2000 (NWDP resource)
sources.what_it_provides: 23,703,774 bytes, 134,069 rows. Periyar rows = 19,588. NEELEESWARAM 10,884 records starting 1971 (near-complete 365/yr 1972-1977, then 730/yr from 1978 as two readings per day); ARANGALI 8,276; VANDIPERIYAR 428.
sources.relevance: high - gives a 55-year continuous Periyar discharge record when joined to the 2001-2025 file; enough for flood-frequency, rating-curve and Muskingum work on long timescales
sources.download_hint: same pattern as above; join on Station + parse 'Data Acquisition Time' as %d-%m-%Y %H:%M
sources.caveat: Despite the '1950' in the filename, the earliest Periyar record is 1971. Deduplicate against the 2001-2025 file - year 2000 appears in both.

sources.name: Kerala SW manual daily rainfall 1991-2020 (NWDP resource)
sources.what_it_provides: 24,200,224 bytes, 151,429 rows. Actual year span is 2000-2020 (not 1991). 2018 has 8,435 station-days. IDUKKI district 7,462 rows, ERNAKULAM 366. Long-record catchment stations: BOYCE ESTATE (9.56472,76.91056) 2000-2020, Vannapuram (9.93611,76.46333) 2002-2020.
sources.relevance: high - real gauge rainfall inside the Idukki catchment spanning 2018, to force the existing SCS-CN model and to bias-check IMD gridded
sources.last_activity: companion 2021-2025 and 2026-2030 resources exist in the same package
sources.caveat: Titled 1991-2020, actually starts 2000. Only 2 of the 7 Idukki/Ernakulam stations have multi-year records - Neriyamangalam and Boothathankettu (the Periyar main-stem stations) exist for 2011 ONLY. River/Basin columns are wrong (Kerala stations labelled 'Tapi', 'Balki').

sources.name: Kerala SW manual daily river discharge (NWDP) - NEGATIVE, do not trust the label
sources.what_it_provides: Advertised as 'River Discharge Kerala_SW Kerala (2001 - 2025) Manual Daily'. Actually 765,060 bytes, 4,904 rows, ALL from calendar year 2011, 23 stations, ZERO Periyar rows.
sources.relevance: low - recorded so nobody else wastes a day on the promising title; it is the state-agency twin of the useful CWC file and looks identical in the catalogue
sources.last_activity: listed as current but content frozen at 2011
sources.caveat: Worked example of the NWDP metadata problem. Stations are also mislabelled with rivers from other states (Narmada, Mahi, Luni, Kim, Banas, Kumaradhara). Use the CWC Kerala file instead.

sources.name: RAT 3.0 Kerala live dashboard (CWRDM + UW SASWE + NASA)
sources.what_it_provides: Satellite + VIC reservoir monitoring for 19 Kerala reservoirs including Idukki (9.845,76.968) and Idamalayaar (10.222,76.706). Products per dam: inflow, outflow, area-elevation curve, TMS-OS surface area, storage change (dels), evaporation. Served as plain static CSVs, no auth.
sources.relevance: high - the only downloadable daily Idukki/Idamalayar inflow series that spans 2018, plus a free area-elevation curve to sanity-check AquaSync's level-storage power law
sources.license: not stated on the portal; RAT engine itself is GPL-3.0
sources.last_activity: data ends 2025-02-22, so the Kerala instance is ~18 months stale as of Aug 2026
sources.caveat: Bare IP over plain HTTP on port 8080 - no TLS, so it will fail any HTTPS-only fetcher (this is why WebFetch errored with WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER; curl works). Fragile hosting: an IP change kills every link. Mirror the CSVs locally now.

sources.name: RAT Kerala - Idukki daily inflow CSV
sources.what_it_provides: 100,264 bytes, 3,410 daily rows, columns date,streamflow (m3/s), 2015-10-24 to 2025-02-22, unbroken. August 2018 complete (31/31 days). Idamalayar twin at .../inflow/idamalayaar.csv, same span.
sources.relevance: high - directly fills 'no pre-2020 Idukki data' as a MODELLED series; usable as a prior or for antecedent-moisture initialisation, not as ground truth
sources.caveat: VERIFIED MISMATCH at the event that matters: RAT Aug-2018 peak 1104.6 m3/s on the 18th vs CWC-observed 2532 cumec at 22:00 on the 15th (2.3x low, 3 days late). RAT gives only 309.9 m3/s on 15 Aug when CWC reports a 1640 cumec daily-average inflow. This is VIC output forced by IMERG, uncalibrated for Idukki (Mullaperiyar transfers upstream are unmodelled in the plain series). Published Idukki skill is r=0.63, RMSE 217.9 m3/s.

sources.name: RAT Kerala - Idukki area-elevation curve (AEC)
sources.what_it_provides: 626 rows at 1 m elevation steps, 551 m to 1176 m, columns elevation,area(km2). Idukki: 50.015 km2 @730 m, 51.098 @731, 52.125 @732, 53.201 @733. Idamalayar twin has 588 rows, 62-649 m: 30.159 @167, 30.414 @168, 30.666 @169 (FRL).
sources.relevance: high - an independent hypsometric curve to cross-validate AquaSync's r2=0.9957 level-storage power law, and to convert satellite surface area into storage
sources.caveat: DEM-derived, and it disagrees with the literature at FRL: it gives 52.1 km2 at 732 m whereas Suresh et al. 2024 Table 1 lists Idukki as 60 km2 at FRL - roughly 13% low. Idamalayar is the opposite sign (30.7 km2 vs 28.3 km2 published, ~8% high). Rescale before use; do not adopt it as an absolute.

sources.name: RAT Kerala - Idukki TMS-OS surface area and storage change
sources.what_it_provides: 657 rows 2017-07-29 to 2025-02-21 (85 observations in 2018), columns date,area (km2). Paired storage change at /dels/idukki.csv, columns date,dS (m3). Optical (MNDWI/NDWI) fused with SAR.
sources.relevance: medium - real satellite observation of Idukki through 2018, but see caveat; more trustworthy in the dry season than the monsoon
sources.caveat: THE AUGUST 2018 VALUES ARE NOT REAL OBSERVATIONS. Area reads 46.2 km2 on 12 Aug then an identical 44.373 km2 on 17, 22 AND 27 Aug - a carried-forward value under monsoon cloud. It also implies the reservoir SHRANK while CWC records it filling to FRL 732.43 m at 01:00 on 17 Aug. The paired dels shows a spurious -102.8 Mm3 on 17 Aug. The RAT paper itself flags 'perennial high cloud cover' as the core limitation. Discard Idukki monsoon-2018 surface area.

sources.name: CWC Reservoir Level & Storage Bulletin archive
sources.what_it_provides: Weekly (Thursday) PDF bulletins covering 161 major Indian reservoirs, Idukki and Idamalayar among them. Per-reservoir fields: FRL (m), live capacity (BCM), bulletin date, current level (m), current live storage (BCM), % of capacity, same-week-last-year %, 10-year-average %, irrigation benefit (000 ha), installed hydropower (MW). Paginated ?page=0..~25; page 20 still lists April 2015.
sources.relevance: high - the only official numeric Idukki level+storage series I could actually retrieve for 2018, and the only one that also carries Idamalayar
sources.license: Government of India, free to reuse
sources.download_hint: Scrape pages 11-16 for 2018: curl -s 'https://cwc.gov.in/en/reservoir-level-storage-bulletin?page=13' | grep -o 'href="[^"]*\.pdf"'  - then pypdf + regex 'IDUKKI\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)\s+([\d.]+)'
sources.caveat: Weekly only - far too coarse to constrain a flood-routing model. Filenames are wildly inconsistent (DD.MM.YYYYcwcbull.pdf, ..._1.pdf, ..._0.pdf, cwcbulletinDD.MM.YYYY.pdf, DD.MM.YYYYcwc.pdf), so you must scrape the listing, not construct URLs. 7 of 52 weeks of 2018 are absent including BOTH flood-week bulletins (09 and 16 Aug 2018) - I tried 7 filename variants, all 404.

sources.name: CWC weekly bulletin, 02 August 2018 (worked example)
sources.what_it_provides: 539,052 bytes. Verified extracted row: 'IDUKKI 732.43 730.25 1.460 1.338 01-08-2018 92 23 41 - 780' = FRL 732.43 m, level 730.25 m, live cap 1.460 BCM, live storage 1.338 BCM, 92% full, 23% same week last year, 41% ten-year average, 780 MW. Sister bulletins verified: 23.08.2018 -> 731.69 m / 1.417 BCM / 97%; 30.08.2018 -> 730.50 m / 1.352 BCM / 93%.
sources.relevance: high - concrete proof the 2018 Idukki level/storage numbers are retrievable, and the FRL and 1.460 BCM live capacity independently confirm AquaSync's constants
sources.download_hint: curl -o b.pdf 'https://cwc.gov.in/sites/default/files/02.08.2018cwcbull_1.pdf' && python -c "from pypdf import PdfReader; import re; t='\n'.join(p.extract_text() for p in PdfReader('b.pdf').pages); print(re.search(r'IDUKKI.{0,180}',t).group())"
sources.caveat: Idukki appears twice per bulletin in two different table layouts (state table and the 161-reservoir national table) - anchor your regex or you will silently parse the wrong column order.

sources.name: CWC 'Kerala Floods of August 2018' study report (via KSDMA)
sources.what_it_provides: 48 pages, 6,003,314 bytes. THE primary source (it is reference 4 of the Current Science paper). Verified quantitative content: Idukki peak inflow 2532 cumec at 22:00 on 15-08-2018; release 1614 cumec (1500 spill + 114 powerhouse); level 730.88 m at 18:00 on 14-08-2018; FRL 732.43 m reached 01:00 on 17-08-2018; peak attenuated 2532 -> 1500 cumec (~41%); 15-17 Aug totals 345 MCM spill + 30 MCM powerhouse against 435 MCM inflow, 60 MCM absorbed; Neeleswaram observed flood peak ~8800 cumec; Idamalayar live storage 1018 MCM, level 168.06 m on 08-08-2018, FRL 169.0 m, MWL 170.3 m, only 60 MCM of flood space; Idamalayar peak release 1272 cumec; design floods 5013 cumec (Idukki) and 3012 cumec (Idamalayar).
sources.relevance: high - the authoritative 2018 numbers, and the correct calibration/validation targets for any AquaSync 2018 replay
sources.download_hint: curl -o cwc2018.pdf '<this url>' ; pypdf extracts 72,025 chars of clean text
sources.caveat: Fig.4 (Idukki inflow/outflow/level) and Fig.5 (Idamalayar) are CHARTS - there is no data table and no annexure. BUT the x-axis tick labels extract as PDF text (09-08-18 12:00 ... 18-08-18 06:00 at 7-hour steps), proving it is a vector Excel plot, so the series are recoverable by SVG path extraction (pdftocairo -svg) rather than pixel digitising. That is the cheapest realistic path to a 2018 hourly Idukki hydrograph.

sources.name: Sudheer et al. 2019, 'Role of dams on the floods of August 2018 in Periyar River Basin, Kerala', Current Science 116(5):780-794
sources.what_it_provides: Free full PDF, 15 pages, 4,413,605 bytes. HEC-HMS reconstruction of the whole Periyar basin. Verified numbers: simulated Idukki peak inflow 2763 m3/s at 20:00 on 15-08-2018 vs measured 2532 m3/s; simulated max release 1860 vs measured 1614 m3/s at 22:00; at L2 (= the Neeleeswaram CWC site) simulated 9965 vs observed 8800 m3/s; virgin (no-dam) simulation gives 8224 m3/s at L1 and 11,990 m3/s at L2; only 16-21% peak attenuation achievable by pre-emptying. Table 1 lists 14 Periyar dams with type, completion year, length and height.
sources.relevance: high - the closest published analogue to what AquaSync's optimiser does, and its 16-21% attenuation ceiling is the number AquaSync's policy search should be benchmarked against
sources.caveat: NO DATA TABLE of any hydrograph. The observed 6-hourly Idukki inflow/release appears only inside Fig.6a and is cited to the CWC report. The paper acknowledges KSEB and CWRDM Kottayam supplied the underlying data - it does not redistribute it.

sources.name: Suresh et al. 2024, RSE - free full manuscript on NASA NTRS
sources.what_it_provides: 56 pages, 3,714,034 bytes - the accepted manuscript of the paywalled Remote Sensing of Environment paper (DOI 10.1016/j.rse.2024.114149), free. Contains the full 19-reservoir table with coordinates and FRL surface areas (Idukki 60 km2, Idamalayaar 28.3 km2), Table 4 inflow validation (Idukki r=0.63, RMSE 217.94 cumecs, nRMSE 12.45%; Idamalayaar r=0.81, RMSE 135.29; Kakki r=0.83; Banasurasagar r=0.78) and Table 5 (Idukki May-Oct 2018 vs KSEB observed: VIC r=0.80/RMSE 170.3/MAE 115.1/KGE 0.59/NSE 0.603; ResORR-regulated r=0.84/RMSE 153.17/MAE 102.32/KGE 0.63/NSE 0.68).
sources.relevance: high - gives the exact, citable error bars for the RAT inflow series AquaSync would ingest, and documents that KSEB holds and shares observed 2018 Idukki inflow
sources.caveat: Accepted manuscript, so figure numbering may differ slightly from the published version. The observed KSEB series it validates against is NOT included as a supplement - only the statistics are published.

sources.name: Minocha et al. 2024, 'Reservoir Assessment Tool version 3.0', Geoscientific Model Development 17:3137
sources.what_it_provides: Open-access description of the RAT 3.0 software platform: VIC hydrological model + MetSim + routing, IMERG forcing, TMS-OS surface area, GEE backend. Crossref-verified: published 2024-04-23, 6 citations.
sources.relevance: medium - the method paper you need if AquaSync ever runs its own RAT instance over the Periyar rather than consuming CWRDM's stale CSVs
sources.caveat: Software paper, contains no Kerala data itself.

sources.name: UW-SASWE/RAT (Reservoir Assessment Tool source)
sources.what_it_provides: Python implementation of RAT 3.0 - VIC + MetSim + routing + Google Earth Engine surface-area extraction, producing inflow, outflow, storage change, evaporation and AEC per reservoir.
sources.relevance: medium - running it yourself over the Periyar with IMD rather than IMERG forcing, and with Mullaperiyar transfers represented, would plausibly beat the r=0.63 Idukki inflow that CWRDM publishes
sources.download_hint: Docs at https://rat-satellitedams.readthedocs.io/ (200); global instance at https://www.satellitedams.net/ (200)
sources.caveat: Only 26 stars and GPL-3.0, which is a licence constraint if AquaSync ships closed. Heavy stack: needs a Google Earth Engine service account plus VIC/MetSim compiled. Realistically a week to a first Periyar run, not a day.

sources.name: IMD 0.25-degree daily gridded rainfall - direct POST endpoint
sources.what_it_provides: The form action behind the IMD download page. POST body RF25=<year> returns one NetCDF per year. VERIFIED LIVE: RF25=2018 gave HTTP 200, 25,431,832 bytes, CDF-1 classic NetCDF, variables LONGITUDE(135), LATITUDE(129), TIME(365, 'days since 1900-12-31'), RAINFALL(365,129,135) in mm. Grid 6.5-38.5N, 66.5-100.0E at 0.25 deg. Years 1901-2024.
sources.relevance: high - the long-record rainfall forcing AquaSync's SCS-CN model needs for any pre-2020 replay; free, instant, no account
sources.license: IMD open data (cite Pai et al. 2014)
sources.last_activity: extended annually; 2024 is the latest full year
sources.download_hint: curl -X POST -d 'RF25=2018' https://www.imdpune.gov.in/cmpg/Griddata/RF25.php -o RF25_2018.nc   # then scipy.io.netcdf_file, cell (9.75N, 77.00E) is nearest Idukki
sources.caveat: 0.25 deg is ~28 km - the Idukki catchment (~1240 km2 incl. free catchment) is only a handful of cells, so orographic gradients across the Western Ghats are smeared. Verified Aug-2018 at the Idukki cell: 203.5 mm on the 9th, 153.3 and 201.8 mm on the 15th-16th, annual total 4048.9 mm. Missing values are coded -999; mask before summing.

sources.name: IMD gridded rainfall NetCDF landing page
sources.what_it_provides: Human-facing year-picker for the 0.25 deg 1901-2024 daily rainfall product; documents the 135x129 grid layout and mm units. Contact for the group: cmagpune@gmail.com.
sources.relevance: medium - the citable landing page; the actual bytes come from RF25.php above
sources.caveat: Page itself exposes no download URLs to a scraper - you must know the RF25.php action. Sibling products exist for 1.0 deg rainfall and for GPM-merged rainfall.

sources.name: imdlib (Python client for IMD gridded data)
sources.what_it_provides: Downloads and parses IMD gridded rainfall and temperature into xarray; handles the binary GRD variants as well as NetCDF. Version 0.1.21, MIT licensed.
sources.relevance: medium - saves writing the NetCDF/GRD parsing, though the raw curl above is a one-liner and avoids a dependency
sources.last_activity: PyPI release 2025-12-04; repo github.com/iamsaswata/imdlib last push 2026-04-02
sources.caveat: Small project (43 stars). Its download routines break whenever IMD changes the form endpoint - verify against the raw curl before trusting it.

sources.name: GUARDIAN: ExtendinG SUb-DAily River Discharge data over INdia (Scientific Data, 2024)
sources.what_it_provides: Hourly (monsoon Jun-Sep) and sub-daily (non-monsoon) discharge for 210 CWC stations, 2020 to present, built by scraping water-surface elevation off the CWC flood portal and applying station rating curves. >800,000 discharge points per year, >4,000 per station per year. Crossref-verified 2024-10-18, 5 citations.
sources.relevance: high - the practical answer to AquaSync gap #2 (Muskingum K and x never gauge-calibrated); hourly Neeleeswaram from 2020 overlaps the amith-vp KSEB release feed exactly
sources.download_hint: See the figshare entry below for the actual files
sources.caveat: STARTS 2020 - it does nothing for the 2018 gap. Discharge is rating-curve-derived, not measured, so it inherits rating error (Neeleeswaram monsoon NSE only 0.765, RMSE 170.7 m3/s).

sources.name: GUARDIAN data on figshare (data.rar + rating curves)
sources.what_it_provides: Two files, confirmed via the figshare API (article 27004282, published 2024-10-19): data.rar 577.0 MB (extended WSE + extended discharge per station) and RC.xlsx 0.1 MB (rating curves). I downloaded RC.xlsx (53,652 bytes, 211 rows) and confirmed all three Periyar gauges: NEELEESWARAM (10.18361,76.49556) monsoon cubic-poly p1=10.6979 p2=198.7671 p3=33.5397, NSE 0.7654, RMSE 170.69, N=2273; non-monsoon p1=6.7636 p2=228.9940 p3=-36.1573, NSE 0.7861, RMSE 127.51, N=6552. ARANGALI monsoon NSE 0.9218 RMSE 42.10. VANDIPERIYAR power-law form, monsoon NSE 0.9476 RMSE 4.04.
sources.relevance: high - the rating curves alone (0.1 MB) let AquaSync convert any CWC stage reading to Periyar discharge, and the 577 MB archive gives hourly Neeleeswaram hydrographs for Muskingum fitting
sources.license: figshare API reports no licence field set - clarify before redistributing
sources.download_hint: RC only (small): curl -L -o RC.xlsx https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/49150798 ; full archive: curl -L -o data.rar https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/49150774
sources.caveat: HTTP 202 is figshare's normal async-landing response, not an error - the ndownloader links return 200. Archive is .rar, needs unrar/7z. VANDIPERIYAR's coordinates here (9.1525,77.1525) DISAGREE with the CWC NWDP file (9.57333,77.09056) by ~46 km - resolve before joining the two sources.

sources.name: GHI: Geospatial dataset for hydrologic analyses in India (ESSD 15:4389, 2023)
sources.what_it_provides: Quality-controlled CWC river gauges with catchment boundaries and hydrometeorological time series over 71 water years (1950-2020). Of 645 CWC stations screened: 213 Group-1 (reliable metadata + adequate daily streamflow), 259 Group-2, 173 rejected. Explicitly mentions the Periyar River and the West-Flowing-Rivers-South basin (coastal Kerala). Crossref-verified 2023-10-05, 17 citations.
sources.relevance: high - delineated catchment polygons for the Periyar CWC gauges would let AquaSync define Muskingum reaches and SCS-CN sub-catchments on a published basis rather than by geometry estimate
sources.caveat: The data itself is on Zenodo, which returned 403 'unusual traffic from your network' for EVERY Zenodo URL I tried from this machine. The paper page is readable; the download needs a different network or a mirror. Also I could NOT confirm Neeleeswaram is in the 213-station Group 1 without opening the archive - verify before relying on it.

sources.name: CAMELS-IND (ESSD 17:461, 2025)
sources.what_it_provides: 472 Peninsular-India catchments (228 with observed streamflow for >30% of 1980-2020), 1 Jan 1980 - 31 Dec 2020 daily. 19 meteorological forcings (precip, tmax/tmin, LW/SW radiation, U/V wind, RH, canopy and soil evaporation, actual and potential ET, soil moisture at 4 depths to 3 m), observed streamflow where available, plus LSTM-predicted streamflow for all 472. Catchment attributes include number of dams, dam volume, population density, urban/agri land-cover change. Crossref-verified 2025-02-05, 23 citations. Built on CWC gauges from India-WRIS using GHI catchment boundaries.
sources.relevance: medium-high - a ready large-sample training set if AquaSync attacks gap #3 (perfect-foresight assumption) with a learned inflow forecaster; the LSTM benchmark is a fair baseline to beat
sources.caveat: Zenodo returned 403 from this network for every attempt (doi.org redirect, /records/, and the /api/records/ JSON endpoint), so I could NOT open the archive to confirm which - if any - Periyar catchments are included. The paper says 'Peninsular India' and 15 CWC interstate basins, which includes Kerala's west-flowing rivers, but names no Kerala catchment. Ends 2020, so it does not carry 2018 Idukki operations - only catchment-scale forcing and streamflow.

sources.name: Mishra et al., 'The Kerala flood of 2018: combined impact of extreme rainfall and reservoir storage' (HESS Discussions preprint)
sources.what_it_provides: Open preprint with full PDF. Establishes that 1-15 day August 2018 rainfall upstream of Idukki, Kakki and Periyar reservoirs had >500-year return periods, and that 6 of 7 major Kerala reservoirs were above 90% of capacity on 8 August 2018. States that Idukki reservoir storage for 2018 was obtained from India-WRIS for 1 Jan - 8 Aug 2018 only.
sources.relevance: medium - useful for antecedent-condition framing and it independently confirms India-WRIS once served daily Idukki storage back to at least 2018
sources.last_activity: 2018 preprint; remained in Discussions, not a final HESS paper
sources.caveat: Preprint only - never completed HESS peer review, so cite with care. Its Idukki storage series stops on 8 August 2018, i.e. it stops one week BEFORE the flood. No supplementary data table of the reservoir series is provided.

sources.name: India-WRIS API contract, recovered from WRIS_India_data_extractor source
sources.what_it_provides: Flask app that wraps the undocumented India-WRIS endpoints. Reading the source gives the complete, otherwise-undocumented contract: POST https://indiawris.gov.in/DataSet/DataSetList ; POST /masterState/StateList {datasetcode} ; POST /masterDistrict/getDistrictbyState {statecode,datasetcode} ; POST /basin/getMasterBasin {datasetcode} ; POST /masterTributary/getMasterTributary {basincode,datasetcode} ; POST /masterAgency/AgencyListInAnyCase ; and the data calls POST /Dataset/{Name}?agencyName=&stateName=&districtName= or POST /Dataset/Basin/{Name}?agencyName=&basinName=&tributaryName= with body {startdate,enddate,size:1000,download:true,page:N}. Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded; Referer https://indiawris.gov.in/dataSet/ required; dataset names are URL-encoded with special cases 'RainFall', 'River%20WaterLevel', 'SnowFall'. No API key, no registration.
sources.relevance: medium - the endpoint spec is worth keeping even though the host is unreachable from here; if indiawris.gov.in is reachable from a machine in India this is a same-day integration
sources.caveat: 0 stars, one-week-old project, no licence, effectively unmaintained. AND the target host is dead from this network - see dead_ends. The repo's own README concedes it exists to 'bypass the issues with swagger UI', i.e. the official Swagger at indiawris.gov.in/swagger-ui/index.html is itself unreliable.

sources.name: amith-vp/Kerala-Dam-Water-Levels (already in AquaSync - refreshed metrics)
sources.what_it_provides: KSEB + Irrigation bulletin scrape, live and historical JSON, GitHub Actions updated. Confirmed via authenticated GitHub API today: 54 stars, last push 2026-08-26T08:05:16Z (same day), repo size 112,128 KB.
sources.relevance: high - already integrated; recorded here only to confirm it is still actively pushing and to fix the 2018 claim
sources.license: NONE DECLARED (GitHub API returns license: null)
sources.download_hint: already wired into the AquaSync loader
sources.caveat: CONFIRMS THE PROJECT'S EXISTING FINDING: this repo cannot contain 2018 data - GitHub Actions only began populating it in Aug 2020. Separately, note it declares NO LICENCE, so redistribution rights are unclear if AquaSync ever ships the cached data.

sources.name: GloLakes: water storage dynamics for 27,000 lakes, 1984-present (ESSD 16:201, 2024)
sources.what_it_provides: Relative and absolute water storage time series from radar altimetry (Topex/Poseidon, Jason-1/2/3, Sentinel-3/6), ICESat-2 laser altimetry and Landsat/Sentinel-2 optical, 1984 to present. Crossref-verified 2024-01-11, 46 citations - the most-cited global reservoir storage dataset found.
sources.relevance: medium - a genuinely independent satellite storage series that spans 2018, worth cross-checking against RAT and the CWC bulletins IF Idukki is among the 27,000
sources.download_hint: Data DOI 10.25914/K8ZF-6G46 -> resolves 200 to NCI Australia GeoNetwork (geonetwork.nci.org.au)
sources.caveat: I could NOT confirm Idukki or Idamalayar are in the 27,000 - the NCI GeoNetwork landing page is a JS catalogue and I did not open the archive. Radar altimetry needs a satellite ground track over the lake; Idukki is a narrow, steep-sided arch-dam reservoir (~52-60 km2) in mountainous terrain, which is exactly the geometry altimetry handles worst. Treat as unverified for these two dams.

sources.name: Global Reservoir Surface Area Dataset (GRSAD)
sources.what_it_provides: Monthly Landsat-derived surface area for 6,817 global reservoirs (GRanD-matched) with cloud/shadow/SLC-off contamination repaired. March 1984 - October 2015.
sources.relevance: low - ENDS OCTOBER 2015, so it cannot see 2018 at all; listed only to close the question
sources.last_activity: static; superseded by GloLakes and ReaLSAT
sources.caveat: Hard stop at 2015-10 makes it useless for the 2018 event. Monthly resolution is in any case far too coarse for flood routing. Its only AquaSync value would be a long pre-2015 Idukki area baseline to extend the RAT AEC calibration.

sources.name: KSDMA dam water level page
sources.what_it_provides: Kerala State Disaster Management Authority's daily water-level page for major KSEB and Irrigation dams; also hosts the mirrored CWC 2018 flood report and a /floods_2018/ section (verified 200).
sources.relevance: medium - KSDMA is the institutional owner and the most likely formal counterparty for a data request; the site itself is the mirror that makes the CWC 2018 report freely reachable
sources.caveat: Presents current levels only - no historical archive, no API, no bulk download. This is the same source the amith-vp scraper consumes, so it adds no data AquaSync does not already have; its value is as a contact route and as the CWC report mirror.

sources.name: CWRDM - Centre for Water Resources Development and Management, Kerala
sources.what_it_provides: Kerala state R&D institute under KSCSTE that co-developed RAT 3.0 Kerala with UW SASWE under NASA grant 80NSSC22K0918. Hosts the RAT-Kerala dashboard and its documentation.
sources.relevance: high - as an institutional route this is the best lead for AquaSync gaps #1 and #5: CWRDM already holds KSEB in-situ 2018 inflow (it is what RAT was calibrated against) and already has a working KSEB/state relationship
sources.last_activity: live; RAT-Kerala data last updated Feb 2025
sources.caveat: No data is published by CWRDM directly beyond the RAT dashboard CSVs - obtaining the underlying KSEB 2018 series requires a formal request. CWRDM Kottayam Sub Centre (Dr George Abe) is separately acknowledged in Sudheer et al. 2019 as the supplier of historic rainfall data, which corroborates that this is a working channel.

dead_ends: indiawris.gov.in IS COMPLETELY UNREACHABLE from this network - not slow, dead. DNS resolves fine (164.100.85.36) but TCP connect never completes: 21 s to timeout, curl exit 28, HTTP code 000. Tested https://indiawris.gov.in/, http://indiawris.gov.in/, https://www.indiawris.gov.in/, https://indiawris.gov.in/wris/, https://indiawris.gov.in/swagger-ui/index.html, https://indiawris.gov.in/v3/api-docs and https://arc.indiawris.gov.in/ - all 000. Meanwhile nwdp.nwic.gov.in, cwc.gov.in and sdma.kerala.gov.in all returned 200 from the same machine, so this is specific to that host, most likely a geo-block on non-Indian IPs. DO NOT plan an India-WRIS dependency without first testing reachability from the actual deployment network. Use NWDP instead - it serves the same CWC data over a working open API.

NWDP HAS NO KERALA RESERVOIR LEVEL OR STORAGE DATA AT ALL. I enumerated all 555 packages. Of 70 'reservoir' packages, 62 are reservoir_discharge_*_telemetry_hourly for individual dams in MP, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Telangana, UP, WB, Uttarakhand and Punjab - not one is in Kerala. The only reservoir level/storage packages are for Andhra Pradesh, BBMB Chandigarh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, and a CWC one. I opened the CWC package (reservoir-water-level-manual-daily-centre-water-commission_cwc): its 4 resources are Odisha storage and Madhya Pradesh water level ONLY. So Idukki and Idamalayar level/storage are definitively NOT on NWDP in any form.

data.gov.in is currently serving a SANDBOX banner and its API is broken for this dataset. The page https://www.data.gov.in/resource/daily-data-reservoir-level-central-water-commission-cwc returns 200 to curl but 403 to WebFetch, is a JS shell, and carries the literal text 'This is a sandbox environment created for testing and demonstration purposes only. The content, data, and functionality may be incomplete or inaccurate.' The only resource id on the page is 579b464db66ec23bdd000001cdc3b564; calling https://api.data.gov.in/resource/579b464db66ec23bdd000001cdc3b564 with the standard public demo key returns {"message":"Meta not found","status":"error","total":0,"records":[]}. kerala.data.gov.in/catalog/reservoir returns 000 (host unreachable). Do not build on data.gov.in.

ZENODO IS 403 FROM THIS NETWORK - which blocks two otherwise-excellent datasets. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14005378 (CAMELS-IND), https://zenodo.org/records/14005378, https://zenodo.org/api/records/14005378 and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7563599 (GHI) all return 403 with the body 'Access to this resource has been restricted due to unusual traffic from your network.' The papers on essd.copernicus.org are readable (200); only the data host is blocked. Retry from a different IP - this is not a broken DOI.

ffs.india-water.gov.in (CWC flood forecasting) has NO usable historical archive or API surface. Root returns 200 but it is an Angular SPA (styles.23a61c3e13ab6949c945.css, Kendo UI) with zero crawlable sub-paths: /ffs, /reservoir, /reservoir-level, /ReservoirLevel, /flood-forecast, /api, /dashboard, /static and /home ALL return 404. It serves live forecasts only. The one thing it is good for is being the upstream that GUARDIAN scraped - and GUARDIAN's output only starts in 2020, which tells you the portal's own retention does not reach 2018.

The two CWC weekly bulletins covering the 2018 flood peak DO NOT EXIST in the public archive. 45 of 52 Thursdays in 2018 are listed and downloadable, but 2018-08-09 and 2018-08-16 are absent (as are 03-29, 05-10, 09-27, 10-18, 12-27). I tried seven filename variants for each - 09.08.2018cwcbull.pdf, 09.08.2018cwcbull_1.pdf, 09.08.2018cwc.pdf, 09.08.2018_0.pdf, 09.08.2018cwcbull_0.pdf, cwcbulletin09.08.2018.pdf and the 16.08 equivalents - every one returned 404. Do not spend time guessing more names; scrape the listing pages (?page=11..16) instead and accept the hole.
GRSAD (Global Reservoir Surface Area Dataset) ENDS OCTOBER 2015 and is monthly. It cannot see the 2018 flood, and monthly resolution is useless for routing regardless. Ruled out.

GRDC (Global Runoff Data Centre) is not a route to Indian discharge. The portal is up (portal.grdc.bafg.de 200) but the literature is explicit that GRDC and RivDIS hold only legacy data for a small fraction of CWC stations, with no provenance and unknown gaps, and that CWC classifies transboundary-basin data. Two catalogue URLs I tried are also dead: grdc.bafg.de/SharedDocs/ExterneLinks/GRDC/grdc_station_catalogue.html and grdc.bafg.de/products/station_catalogue/station_catalogue/ both 404. Use NWDP for Indian gauges instead - it has 55 years of Periyar data GRDC does not.

keralafloodwatch.in and dams.keralam.co are LIVE DASHBOARDS ONLY (both 200). keralafloodwatch shows current Idukki and Idamalayar storage percentages and gate status and names IMD/CWC/KSDMA/KSEB as sources, but exposes no API, no bulk download, and no confirmed pre-2020 archive. They re-present data AquaSync already ingests via amith-vp. No new information.

MDPI and ScienceDirect both 403 this network, so several promising papers could not be read directly: https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4441/15/7/1371 (403), https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0034425724001603 (403), https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2214581825000862 (403). These are BOT BLOCKS, not dead links - I confirmed 10.3390/w15071371 and 10.1016/j.rse.2024.114149 are real via the Crossref API. For the RSE paper use the free NASA NTRS manuscript listed in sources; for the MDPI one try a different network.

technologies.name: NWDP CKAN API (nwdp.nwic.gov.in)
technologies.limitations: Dataset titles systematically misstate temporal coverage - one Kerala file labelled '2001-2025' holds only 2011. The River/Basin/Tributary/Subtributary columns are corrupted portal-wide by a bad foreign-key join (Kerala stations tagged 'Narmada', 'Tapi', 'Luni'). Filter on Station name and lat/lon, never on the river fields. Only station-level point data; no reservoir operations for Kerala.
technologies.fit_for_aquasync: Immediate, highest-value integration. One new loader module alongside the existing amith-vp one gets 55 years of Neeleeswaram discharge plus 21 years of Idukki-catchment rainfall. ~1 day to a working ingest: package_show for resource URLs, requests.get the CSV, parse '%d-%m-%Y %H:%M', filter Station in {NEELEESWARAM, VANDIPERIYAR, ARANGALI}.
technologies.recent_updates: Portal carries 2026-2030 forward-dated resources, so it is actively curated as of Aug 2026. No key or registration required.

technologies.name: RAT 3.0 (Reservoir Assessment Tool), UW-SASWE
technologies.limitations: Idukki inflow skill is only r=0.63 / RMSE 217.9 m3/s overall, and peaks are explicitly under-predicted (the paper says so). VIC does not represent the Mullaperiyar transfer into Idukki in the plain series. Optical surface area collapses under monsoon cloud - Aug 2018 Idukki area is a carried-forward constant. Running your own instance needs a Google Earth Engine service account plus compiled VIC/MetSim.
technologies.fit_for_aquasync: Two distinct uses. (a) Consume the CWRDM CSVs today - 30 minutes of curl - for a modelled 2015-2025 Idukki/Idamalayar daily inflow prior covering 2018, plus a free AEC. (b) Longer term, run RAT yourself over the Periyar with IMD gridded forcing instead of IMERG and with Mullaperiyar represented; that is the credible path past r=0.63. Budget a week, not a day, and note GPL-3.0.
technologies.recent_updates: RAT 3.0 published GMD 2024-04-23; repo last push 2026-01-13 (26 stars). ResORR regulation algorithm (Env. Model. Softw. 2024) lifts Idukki 2018 inflow from NSE 0.603 to 0.68 - but the ResORR series is NOT what the Kerala dashboard serves.

technologies.name: CWC weekly reservoir bulletin harvesting
technologies.limitations: Weekly cadence only - useless for sub-daily flood routing. Filenames are inconsistent across five patterns, so URLs must be scraped from the listing, not constructed. 7 of 52 weeks of 2018 are missing including both flood-peak weeks. PDF table extraction needs care because Idukki appears twice per bulletin in two different column layouts.
technologies.fit_for_aquasync: The only official numeric 2018 Idukki AND Idamalayar level+storage series obtainable without an institutional request. Perfect as an independent anchor for a 2018 replay's initial and weekly-checkpoint states, and it independently confirms FRL 732.43 m and 1.460 BCM live capacity. ~half a day: scrape pages 11-16, pypdf, regex, done.
technologies.recent_updates: Archive verified back to April 2015 (page 20); still published every Thursday as of 2025.

technologies.name: IMD 0.25-degree gridded daily rainfall (RF25.php)
technologies.limitations: 0.25 deg is ~28 km, so the Idukki catchment spans only a few cells and the sharp Western Ghats orographic gradient is smeared - expect the gauge-vs-grid mismatch to be the dominant error in any pre-2020 SCS-CN replay. Missing values coded -999. One HTTP request per year, no bulk endpoint.
technologies.fit_for_aquasync: Directly closes the long-record rainfall forcing need for 1901-2024. Verified working with a single unauthenticated POST; 25 MB per year; scipy.io.netcdf_file reads it with no extra dependency. Pair it with the two long-record Kerala SW gauges (BOYCE ESTATE, Vannapuram) for bias correction inside the Idukki catchment.
technologies.recent_updates: Extended annually to 2024. imdlib 0.1.21 (MIT, 43 stars) released 2025-12-04 wraps it, but the raw curl is a one-liner and avoids the dependency.

technologies.name: GUARDIAN rating-curve discharge (hourly, 210 CWC stations)
technologies.limitations: STARTS 2020 - contributes nothing to the 2018 gap. Discharge is inferred from stage via rating curves, so it carries rating error: Neeleeswaram monsoon NSE 0.765 with RMSE 170.7 m3/s, which is large relative to normal flows though modest against an 8800 m3/s flood. Single 577 MB .rar, no API, no versioning, no licence declared. VANDIPERIYAR coordinates conflict with the CWC source by ~46 km.
technologies.fit_for_aquasync: The best available answer to gap #2 (Muskingum K and x never gauge-calibrated). Hourly Neeleeswaram discharge from 2020 overlaps the amith-vp KSEB release feed (2020-08-13 onward), giving matched upstream-release / downstream-response pairs at the timestep the routing model actually runs at. The 53 KB RC.xlsx alone is worth taking immediately.
technologies.recent_updates: Published Scientific Data 2024-10-18; figshare deposit 2024-10-19; 5 citations. Advertised as extending 'to present' but the deposit is a static v1 snapshot.

technologies.name: Vector extraction of the CWC Fig.4 Idukki hydrograph
technologies.limitations: Unproven for this specific PDF - I confirmed the axis tick labels extract as live text (09-08-18 12:00 through 18-08-18 06:00 at 7-hour steps), which shows it is a vector Excel chart rather than a raster image, but I did not attempt the path extraction itself. Success depends on the series being drawn as polylines rather than flattened. Even if it works, the result is a derived reconstruction, not an authoritative record, and must be labelled as such.
technologies.fit_for_aquasync: The cheapest realistic route to a genuine 6-hourly 2018 Idukki inflow/outflow/level hydrograph without an institutional data request - and it validates against known anchors (peak inflow 2532 cumec at 22:00 15 Aug, release 1614, FRL 732.43 m at 01:00 17 Aug) so the reconstruction can be quality-checked rather than taken on faith. Try `pdftocairo -svg` on page 12 first; fall back to WebPlotDigitizer.
technologies.recent_updates: n/a - technique, not a product. The same approach applies to Current Science Fig.6a for a second independent digitisation.

technologies.name: Institutional request to CWRDM / KSEB
technologies.limitations: Not a technical route - timeline is weeks to months and entirely outside your control. No published data-sharing policy or request form was found. Any data obtained will likely carry redistribution restrictions, which matters if AquaSync ships publicly.
technologies.fit_for_aquasync: The ONLY route to genuine observed 2018 Idukki inflow/outflow, and it also addresses gap #5 (no path to KSEB/KSDMA integration) - the same conversation serves both. Three independent teams document that KSEB supplied exactly this: Suresh et al. 2024 calibrated RAT against 'in-situ inflow data obtained from the KSEB' and validated Idukki against 'Observed inflow from KSEB for the period of May - October 2018'; Sudheer et al. 2019 acknowledge KSEB and CWRDM Kottayam; the CWC report used KSEB gate logs. CWRDM is a Kerala state institute that already co-develops RAT-Kerala with NASA funding, so the channel demonstrably exists. Start there, cite the RAT-Kerala collaboration, and ask for the May-Oct 2018 Idukki and Idamalayar series by name.
technologies.recent_updates: RAT-Kerala partnership active under NASA grant 80NSSC22K0918; dashboard data current to Feb 2025.
